It was one of those mornings that just felt important.
The sun rose gently, like it knew something special was about to happen. Members of the Rotary Club of Muthaiga arrived early, smiles wide, hearts full, Rotary pins shining proudly. There was laughter, a few happy nerves, and that shared excitement that comes when a dream is finally becoming real.
For months, this project had lived in meetings, budgets, site visits, and endless WhatsApp updates. But on this day, it stood in bricks, cables, bookshelves, and brand-new screens.
💻 The Computer Lab
When the doors opened, you could actually hear the soft gasp from the students.
Row after row of computers. Clean desks. Proper chairs. A room that whispered possibility. For many of those learners, this was the first time seeing so many computers in one place — not in a movie, not in a photo — but right there, waiting for them.
A Rotarian leaned over and showed one student how to move the mouse. The boy’s face lit up like he had just discovered magic.
Because in a way… he had.
That lab wasn’t just about technology. It was about:
Research for school projects
Learning digital skills
Opening doors to future careers
Confidence to compete in a digital world
Rotary hadn’t just handed over machines. They had handed over access.
📚 The Library
Next was the library — calm, bright, and full of stories waiting to be opened.
Shelves stood proudly, lined with colorful books: storybooks, revision guides, atlases, novels, and learning materials. The room smelled like fresh paint and new pages — the scent of fresh beginnings.

A quiet place to dream
A safe place to learn
A space where imagination grows
A tool for academic success

Our guest speaker this week is  Hon. Soipan Tuya , Cabinet Secretary for Defence of the Republic of Kenya. 

A distinguished lawyer and Advocate of the High Court, she holds an LLB from the University of Nairobi and an LLM in Sustainable International Development from the University of Washington.

She currently serves as the principal advisor to the President on defence matters and chairs the Defence Council.

As the former Cabinet Secretary for Environment, she launched the 15 Billion National Tree Growing Programme to reach 30% tree cover by 2032.

Additionally, she successfully co-hosted the inaugural Africa Climate Summit in 2023, leading to the Nairobi Declaration.

She served as a two-term MP for Narok County and she has dedicated 18 years to legal advocacy and free representation for vulnerable women and children in pastoralist communities.

Hon. Tuya’s career is defined by her commitment to national security, environmental sustainability, and the economic empowerment of all Kenyans.

💧 SOKONI WATER PROJECT – HOMABAY COUNTY💧

Clean water is not a luxury. It is dignity. It is health. It is opportunity.

This past week, we have celebrated the impact of the Sokoni Water Project in Homa Bay County — a project that has touched hundreds of lives in Sokoni area by providing safe and reliable access to clean water.

Before this project, many women walked long distances in search of water. Now, children spend more time in school, families are healthier - with a new baby to show for it, and locals are spending more time on economic activities.

This is what service looks like.
This is what partnership makes possible.
This is Rotary in action.

Thank you to every Rotarian, our partners in RC Peachtree City and Sokoni Women’s Development Initiative, and every supporter who made this a reality. Together, we are not just providing water — we are restoring hope and building a stronger community. 💙

Needs Assessment Series, Part 3/3

We closed off January on 30th January 2026 with our final needs assessment of the month, visiting Little Heaven Daycare Centre, a project under the High Five Initiative, in Kibera.

Little Heaven exists to solve a quiet but urgent problem in informal settlements, safe and reliable childcare. For many parents seeking daily casual work, the absence of affordable daycare means children are left locked indoors or exposed to the streets. This centre provides an alternative, a safe space where children are cared for, fed, and engaged in early learning while parents earn a livelihood with peace of mind.

During the visit, we interacted with the children, engaged the volunteers, and learnt more about the centre’s vision to expand childcare services in high-need areas. Currently operating from a rented three-room facility, the centre serves up to 40 children daily, supported by two volunteers and sustained largely through goodwill.

Key needs identified include consistent rent support, food provision, basic renovations, child-friendly furniture, and learning and play materials. These are not luxuries, they are essentials for stability, dignity, and quality care.

As we wrapped up the month, this visit reminded us that impactful work often happens quietly, at the grassroots, where small, consistent support can change daily realities for both children and families.

Needs Assessment Series - Bonus Story 

After our needs assessment at Olturoto Comprehensive School, something quietly powerful happened.

Our very own Rotarian https://t.me/sammybundi looked at the struggling computer room and said, “I can fix this.”

Sammy reminded us of a simple truth, many of us are sitting on solutions without realizing it. That old laptop gathering dust, the broken desktop, the spare keyboard or mouse you wrote off years ago, each carries a small but vital piece of hope. Not everything has to work, sometimes it just has to help something else work.

On Saturday, 31st January, Sammy went back to the school to get his hands dirty. He was joined by support from within our Rotary family, with Rotarian https://t.me/melvink_md volunteering her brother to assist with the repairs. Parts were stripped, swapped, tested, tried again, and tried once more.

The result?
Nine computers brought back to life, and spare parts saved for another day.

This is Rotary at its best. Seeing a gap, stepping forward, and pulling together as a family. Proof that impact does not always need a budget line, sometimes it just needs initiative, skill, and a generous heart.

Thank you, Sammy, for reminding us that service is often practical, hands-on, and powered by togetherness.

#WeAreNgongRoad #UnitedForGood #District9212
